title: Outpatient consultations
short: Consultations for new concerns, follow-up visits and general check-ups.
intro: An outpatient consultation is a visit where you see a clinician, receive an assessment and go home the same day. It is often the first step for a new health concern, a follow-up or a general check-up.
expect: A conversation about your symptoms, health history and concerns.
A clinical assessment, which may include an examination.
Advice on next steps, which may include tests, treatment or referral where needed.
Guidance on when to return and which warning signs to watch for.
for: Adults and children with new or ongoing health concerns
People who want a general check-up or a blood pressure check
Anyone unsure which service they need; we can point you in the right direction
prepare: Bring your medicines, or a list of them.
Bring earlier medical records or test results if you have them.
Write down your symptoms, when they started and your questions.
faqs: Do I need an appointment?
NexaCare welcomes walk-in patients. You can also request an appointment to help us plan your visit. A request is not confirmed until we contact you.
Can I bring a family member?
Many patients come with a relative or friend. Please tell the team if you need extra support with mobility or communication.

title: Maternal and child health
short: Support for women during pregnancy and after birth, and for babies and children as they grow.
intro: Maternal and child health care supports women through pregnancy, birth and the weeks after, and supports babies and children as they grow and develop.
expect: Pregnancy check-ups and advice.
Growth and development checks for babies and children.
Information about childhood vaccination.
Guidance on warning signs and when to seek urgent care.
for: Women who are pregnant or planning a pregnancy
New mothers and their babies
Parents with questions about a child's health, growth or vaccinations
prepare: Bring your antenatal or child health booklet if you have one.
Bring any earlier test results.
Write down questions about feeding, sleep, growth or vaccinations.
faqs: When should antenatal care start?
WHO advises starting antenatal care early in pregnancy and attending regular visits. Call us to talk through your situation.
What if my baby seems very unwell?
Do not wait for an appointment. Difficulty breathing, convulsions, being unable to feed or being very drowsy need urgent care. Go to the nearest health facility.

title: Laboratory services
short: Tests on samples such as blood or urine to support diagnosis and monitoring.
intro: Laboratory services test samples, such as blood or urine, to help clinicians diagnose conditions and monitor treatment. Your clinician decides which tests suit you.
expect: Your clinician explains which test is advised and why.
A sample is collected by staff.
Results are reviewed with you. Some tests take longer than others.
Advice on follow-up if results need action.
for: Patients referred for tests after a consultation
People monitoring a known condition as advised by a clinician
prepare: Ask in advance whether a test needs preparation, such as fasting.
Bring any test request from another clinician.
Tell staff which medicines you take.
faqs: How long do results take?
It depends on the test. Ask the team when your sample is taken.
Can I request a test without seeing a clinician?
Please ask the team about their process. Results are most useful when reviewed with a clinician.

title: Pharmacy
short: Medicines dispensed with clear guidance on using them safely.
intro: The pharmacy supplies medicines prescribed by clinicians and helps you understand how to use them safely.
expect: Medicines dispensed against a prescription.
Guidance on how and when to take your medicine.
Advice on storage and possible side effects.
A chance to ask questions before you leave.
for: Patients with a prescription from a NexaCare clinician or another provider
Anyone with questions about using a medicine safely
prepare: Bring your prescription or medicine list.
Tell the pharmacist about allergies and every medicine you take, including herbal products.
Ask if anything on the label is unclear.
faqs: Can you explain how to take my medicine?
Yes. Ask the pharmacy team to go through the label and instructions with you. Never change a prescribed dose without advice from your prescriber.
Should I stop a medicine when I feel better?
Not without advice. Some medicines, such as antibiotics, must be completed as directed. Ask your prescriber or pharmacist.

title: Family planning
short: Information and support to help you decide whether and when to have children.
intro: Family planning services give information and support so you can decide whether and when to have children, in line with your health, circumstances and values.
expect: A respectful, private conversation about your options.
Information on available methods, benefits and side effects.
Support to choose a method that suits you.
Follow-up and advice if you have concerns.
for: Women and couples planning or spacing pregnancies
Anyone who wants information about contraception
prepare: Think about your questions and preferences beforehand.
Tell the clinician about your health history and medicines.
Bring a partner only if you wish to.
faqs: Is the consultation private?
Health services are expected to protect patient privacy. Ask the team how your information is handled.
Can I come alone?
Many people attend alone. You decide whether to bring a partner.

title: Emergency care
short: Care for sudden, serious illness or injury.
intro: Emergency care is for sudden, serious illness or injury. If you or someone else is in danger, do not wait: go to the nearest emergency facility or call emergency services.
expect: A quick assessment to judge how urgent the problem is.
Immediate care to stabilise a patient where possible.
Advice on further treatment, which may include referral to another facility.
for: People with sudden, severe symptoms
People with injuries that need prompt attention
prepare: Call ahead if you can.
Bring someone who can help give information.
Bring a list of medicines and any records you have.
faqs: What counts as an emergency?
Examples include chest pain, severe difficulty breathing, heavy bleeding, seizures, sudden weakness or confusion, serious injury and pregnancy danger signs. When in doubt, seek help immediately.
Is emergency care available 24 hours?
Please confirm current emergency hours with NexaCare by phone before travelling. In a life-threatening situation, go to the nearest emergency facility.

title: Minor procedures and first aid
short: Treatment for minor injuries and short procedures, with clear aftercare advice.
intro: Minor procedures and first aid cover small, short treatments and immediate care for minor injuries, such as cleaning and dressing a wound.
expect: Assessment of the injury or problem.
An explanation of what the procedure involves.
Wound care and dressing where appropriate.
Aftercare advice, including signs of infection to watch for.
for: People with minor cuts, burns or wounds
Patients who need dressing changes as advised by a clinician
prepare: While travelling, cover a bleeding wound with a clean cloth and press firmly.
Bring your vaccination record if you have one.
Tell staff about any allergies.
faqs: How do I know if a wound needs professional care?
Seek care if bleeding does not stop with firm pressure, the wound is deep or dirty, it was caused by an animal bite, or it shows signs of infection such as spreading redness, swelling, pus or fever.
Which procedures are offered?
Please call and describe the situation in general terms. The team will tell you whether it can be dealt with at the centre.

title: Counselling services
short: A private space to talk through stress, worries and difficult life events.
intro: Counselling offers a private space to talk through stress, worries, relationships or difficult life events with a counsellor.
expect: A respectful, non-judgemental conversation.
Time to explain your concerns at your own pace.
Support to explore ways of coping.
Guidance on further support if it would help.
for: People feeling stressed, anxious or low
Families dealing with illness, loss or change
Carers who need support
prepare: Choose a time when you can talk freely.
Think about what you hope to get from the session.
Ask how sessions work and how your privacy is protected.
faqs: Is counselling the same as medical treatment?
No. Counselling is supportive talking. If a clinician thinks other care could help, they can discuss options with you.
What if I am in crisis?
If you may harm yourself or someone else, get help immediately: contact emergency services, go to the nearest health facility or reach out to someone you trust.

title: Physiotherapy
short: Help to move well after injury, illness or surgery, or with long-term conditions.
intro: Physiotherapy helps people move and function as well as possible after injury, illness or surgery, or when living with a long-term condition that affects movement.
expect: An assessment of movement, strength and pain.
A plan of exercises or techniques suited to you.
Advice on activity, posture and moving safely at home.
Reviews to check your progress.
for: People recovering from injury or illness
Older adults concerned about balance or falls
People with ongoing aches or reduced mobility
prepare: Wear comfortable clothing.
Bring referral notes or scan results if you have them.
Tell the physiotherapist about pain, medicines and health conditions.
faqs: Do I need a referral?
Please ask the team. Bring any notes from other clinicians.
Can physiotherapy be provided at home?
Physiotherapy visits at home may be possible depending on suitability and availability. Ask about them when you enquire about homecare.

title: Homecare
short: Support at home for older adults, people recovering from illness and their families.

title: Telemedicine
short: Speak to a health professional remotely when a visit is not needed or not possible.
intro: Telemedicine lets you speak with a healthcare professional remotely, for example by phone or video, when an in-person visit is not necessary or not possible.
expect: A remote conversation about your concern.
Advice, or a recommendation to attend in person.
Guidance on follow-up.
for: People who find travelling difficult
Patients who need follow-up advice
Anyone who wants initial guidance before a visit
prepare: Choose a quiet, private place.
Check your phone signal or internet connection.
Have your medicines and any recent readings to hand.
faqs: How do I book a telemedicine consultation?
Request an appointment and choose Telemedicine. The team will confirm how the consultation will take place.
Can telemedicine be used in an emergency?
No. Emergencies need in-person care. Go to the nearest emergency facility.
